title: Active accounts retain source-known demo passwords
evidence: runtime-data.json: 173 of 240 active accounts match two seed-script password defaults. Matching active role assignments include 4 super_admin, 3 finance_admin, 3 reviewer and 3 support_agent. Role counts may overlap accounts. No password, hash or account identifier is included in this report.
impact: Knowledge of a source default can permit account takeover, including administrative access. Blocking public self-registration of staff roles does not protect already seeded privileged users. This is the strongest immediate release blocker; no successful attacker access is claimed.
remediation: Identify affected accounts privately; disable unused demo accounts, replace required staff credentials with unique values, revoke their sessions and review authentication/admin history. Separate seed data from the production environment and require explicit safe seeding controls.
acceptance: Zero active production accounts match any seed default. Every retained staff account has a verified owner; existing sessions are revoked after remediation; login and admin access are retested with unique credentials.

title: Daily SQL backup is readable by unrelated local users
evidence: backup-permissions.json: /var/backups/cineconnect is mode 0775 and the 20261014 daily SQL gzip is 0644. runuser -u nobody -- test -r returned true. Current production env and the newer manual audit backup directory are protected; the exposure is the daily backup path.
impact: A compromised application or ordinary account on this shared host can read the database dump, including account hashes, session metadata and application records. This was a readability check, not a download of customer data. Encrypted fields alone do not make the entire SQL archive safe.
remediation: Use a dedicated backup identity, restrictive directory/file permissions and umask 077 in the scheduled job. Encrypt off-host archives and review historical daily backups for the same exposure. Keep current production secrets and rollback backups restricted.
acceptance: An unprivileged account cannot list or read backup contents. A newly scheduled backup has the intended owner/mode, passes integrity checks and can be restored by the recovery operator.

title: Public cinema ignores private project and file visibility
evidence: projects.py:161 and 635: public_cinema filters folder/status/media readiness but not Project.visibility or ProjectFile.visibility. Live anonymous results contained 8 member-only projects and 8 budget values. A private project with a member-only external trailer was returned in the isolated probe.
impact: An authenticated member can create content that is later exposed publicly with project description, budget, schedule and member counts. An external video link being reachable elsewhere does not authorize publication of its surrounding private project metadata.
remediation: Require explicit publication consent and both project/file visibility gates. Use a minimal public serializer that excludes budgets and internal project state by default. Review existing cinema records and publication controls before migration.
acceptance: Anonymous callers see no private/member-only project or file in the cinema feed. Private budgets remain absent even when an owner intentionally publishes a trailer. Negative cases cover external URLs and uploaded files.

title: Safety editing and removed-member checks are inconsistent
evidence: operations.py:124, 1599 and 1624. A read-only member changed risk/status and made a mandatory checklist item optional (HTTP 200). A removed project member created a safety check (HTTP 201). _project_for_member omits member status; update handlers reuse a view-access helper.
impact: View access can be used to falsify operational safety state, and revoked project membership does not consistently stop new safety records. The unrelated-user read check passed, so this is a specific authorization gap rather than unrestricted public access.
remediation: Create distinct read/create/edit/approve policies. Require active membership plus an authorized responsible person or safety role for mutations. Apply the same rule to incidents and checklist items; preserve auditable completion history.
acceptance: Read-only and removed members receive 403/404 on all unauthorized mutations. Owners and assigned safety staff succeed. Tests cover revocation, insurance viewers, reviewers, mandatory-item changes and completion transitions.

title: Payment reviewers can approve their own submitted proof
evidence: payments.py:64 and 577: the decision endpoint checks a finance/admin/reviewer role without checking submitter or booking-party conflicts. An isolated super-admin payer approved their own pending proof with HTTP 200; the posting service creates a receipt and secures the booking.
impact: The manual payment process lacks separation between submission and verification. A privileged participant can mark their own transfer verified without an independent reviewer. This audit did not move money or test a real bank transfer.
remediation: Reject review by the submitter, payer, payee or other disallowed conflicted party. Define an independent reviewer policy and an auditable exceptional approval path if the business requires one. Review whether ordinary reviewer roles should access finance decisions.
acceptance: Self-approval and conflicted approval return 403. A different authorized finance reviewer can approve verified evidence, producing one receipt and balanced expected ledger entries. Concurrent duplicate decisions are tested against MySQL.

title: All proxy clients share loopback rate-limit identity
evidence: extensions.py:15 uses get_remote_address; create_app has no trusted proxy normalization. Nginx proxies via 127.0.0.1. Two different forwarded client IPs both produced the limiter key 127.0.0.1. auth.py applies login 10/minute, registration 20/hour and reset 10/hour limits.
impact: Different users compete for the same per-endpoint quota, making login and registration susceptible to cross-user lockout. Raw forwarded headers are also recorded in auth metadata without trusted normalization. No production limit was deliberately exhausted.
remediation: Configure a precisely trusted proxy boundary and normalize client IP before throttling/audit recording. Use account-aware limits where appropriate and preserve spoofing protection. Do not trust arbitrary caller-supplied X-Forwarded-For values. See reference R1.
acceptance: Two real client addresses have independent quotas; repeated attempts from one address are limited. Forged forwarding headers cannot bypass the policy. Login, registration, reset and uploads retain useful abuse protection.

title: MySQL is reachable on the public server interface
evidence: The host listener is 0.0.0.0:3306 and UFW allows TCP 3306 from Anywhere (IPv4). A TCP connection from this audit workstation to srv951538.hstgr.cloud:3306 succeeded. API and Redis listeners are loopback-only. MySQL app transport currently negotiated TLS.
impact: The database has an unnecessary broad network attack surface for an app running on the same host. TLS is positive but does not replace network access control. This host serves other apps, so database access requirements must be inventoried before restrictions change.
remediation: Restrict database access to loopback/private networking and specifically approved administration sources. Review database host grants and external consumers. Apply changes through a reversible maintenance procedure that preserves other services.
acceptance: Unapproved external connections to 3306 fail; CineConnect and every approved database consumer remain healthy. Approved remote administration uses a controlled tunnel or explicit allowlist.

title: Recovery coverage falls short of the documented targets
evidence: Root cron runs a daily database dump at 02:00 UTC; the latest gzip passed integrity checking. Its script has no storage or off-host copy stage. No scheduled CineConnect storage/off-host job was found in inspected cron/timers. docs/DEPLOYMENT_INPUTS.md specifies 15-minute RPO and 4-hour RTO.
impact: Daily local SQL backups leave up to roughly one day of database change at risk and do not protect against host loss. Uploaded documents need their own coordinated recovery. Recent manual database/storage snapshots and rollback assets help deployment recovery but are not a continuous disaster-recovery system.
remediation: Implement encrypted off-host database backups, appropriate point-in-time recovery and scheduled file backups. Define ownership, retention and alerts. Perform a full isolated restore including encryption keys, uploaded files, migrations and app startup.
acceptance: A timed restore demonstrates the approved RPO/RTO, including a recent upload and transaction. Backup failure alerts reach an owner; restoration succeeds after simulated loss of the original host without using that host as the only key source.

title: Production verification data still contains demo and missing evidence
evidence: data-integrity.json and runtime-data.json: 122 accounts use the demo email domain; 239 private file rows are marked missing. There are 144 document references on approved KYC submissions whose files are missing. There are 102 approved KYC submissions overall. These are counts, not proof of real identity fraud.
impact: Backend-connected records can still be synthetic, incomplete or unsuitable for production trust claims. Approved KYC states without underlying evidence should not authorize real business activity without a documented decision. Historical private-field placeholders also need owner re-entry.
remediation: Classify retained demonstration records, exclude them from real-user discovery/metrics, and migrate only reviewed business data. Re-verify affected identities and request replacement evidence. Preserve required history rather than silently deleting records.
acceptance: Every production-approved KYC decision has accessible authorized evidence or a documented exception. No demo listing is presented as a verified real provider. Missing files and the 18 previously identified private-field placeholders have a tracked disposition.

title: Self-service email verification and password recovery are unavailable
evidence: Live bootstrap reports email=false. SMTP_HOST and SMTP_FROM are unset. The user confirmed no SMTP/SMS/native-push provider is currently configured. Auth email delivery exists in source but cannot operate without the service.
impact: Users can lose account access without a functioning recovery channel. Stronger password rotation for PR-01 requires a safe enrollment/recovery process. This is a known operational dependency, not a claim that the UI falsely reports email delivery.
remediation: Configure a production email provider with authenticated sending and monitored delivery, or formally constrain launch to a staffed verified recovery process. Establish account ownership checks and escalation procedures before onboarding.
acceptance: A real user receives verification and reset messages; tokens expire and are single-use, and link handling works in supported browsers. Delivery failures are observable. An alternative manual process is documented, staffed and demonstrated if chosen.

title: Health checks do not prove end-to-end service operation
evidence: SENTRY_DSN is unset. All three app containers have no Docker health check. /health/ready checks only database and Redis, not queue processing, file scanning, email, disk or scheduler freshness. Containers were running with zero restarts and no API tracebacks/500 lines in the sampled 30 minutes.
impact: The status endpoint can remain green while uploads or notifications stop processing. No tested alert route or on-call acknowledgement was demonstrated. Generic host monitoring snippets exist; their app-specific coverage was not established.
remediation: Add app-specific external probes and alerts for errors, queue age, failed tasks, antivirus freshness, disk, backup age and scheduler activity. Define an on-call owner and response runbook; include a synthetic safe workflow.
acceptance: A controlled staging failure of each critical dependency triggers an actionable alert and recovery runbook. Production monitoring reports freshness and failures without logging credentials or sensitive payloads.

title: Shared-host resource limits and Docker log rotation are absent
evidence: Infrastructure snapshot: root disk 86% used, 28 GiB available; RAM available about 3.1 GiB of 16 GiB; 2 GiB swap fully used. API/worker/scheduler have memory=0, nano_cpus=0, no PID cap and json-file logging without options. No daemon.json logging policy exists.
impact: A busy job, noisy log or another service can consume shared resources and affect multiple apps. Full swap is a capacity warning, not evidence of an outage; current app log files were small. Disk exhaustion would affect uploads, database writes and backups.
remediation: Set measured per-service limits and reserved headroom, log size/count rotation and disk alerts. Review old releases/backups with retention rules and owner approval. Keep evidence and rollback assets required by policy. See reference R2.
acceptance: Limits and rotation appear in running container inspection; a staging resource test degrades safely. Disk growth has a monitored budget and cleanup ownership. Production remains healthy after container recreation.

title: Browser application responses lack protective web headers
evidence: GET / returned no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy. API responses do include these controls. Several static location blocks define their own headers.
impact: The actual page hosting authentication lacks framing and script-source protections even though the API has them. A successful HTTPS visit to the HTML entry point alone does not set HSTS. This audit did not demonstrate a working script-injection exploit.
remediation: Apply tested page headers across all web entry points, accounting for Nginx inheritance. Design a CSP compatible with Flutter, CanvasKit, uploads, media and intended third-party content. Preserve camera/microphone permissions needed by approved workflows.
acceptance: HTML/deep links and assets have the expected headers. Framing is blocked and CSP violations are reviewed in a real browser. Login, media, file selection, camera and exports still work.

title: Editable admin permissions do not govern all admin access
confidence: Confirmed isolated behavior and source review
evidence: admin_control.py:46 uses fixed role membership for most access; the same module exposes editable RolePermission records. A support_agent with zero assigned permissions still received the account directory (HTTP 200). policies.py permission checks are used elsewhere, such as KYC.
impact: Operators may believe removing a permission removes access, while fixed role guards continue to allow it. This is a policy/UI inconsistency; static role access may be intentional, but its precedence must be explicit and tested.
remediation: Define one authoritative role/permission model. Either enforce fine-grained permissions on relevant endpoints or remove misleading configuration for immutable role powers. Review access to user email, finance, reports and moderation separately.
acceptance: A documented role matrix matches API behavior. Removing an editable permission revokes the corresponding capability on the next request; unsupported combinations cannot be saved in the admin UI.

title: Sensitive admin changes are absent from the audit feed
evidence: admin_control.py:338 changes user status and roles without an audit-event write. An isolated account suspension returned 200 but /admin/control/audit-events stayed at zero events. The feed currently combines KYC, booking, payment and moderation history.
impact: Investigators cannot reliably reconstruct who suspended an account or changed staff access using the advertised audit history. Existing event tables do not substitute for coverage of each privileged mutation.
remediation: Record actor, target, before/after state, reason, timestamp and request ID for privileged changes. Cover permissions, fee rules and contract templates as well as users. Apply retention and access rules; avoid secret or document payloads in events.
acceptance: Every tested sensitive admin mutation produces exactly one durable event with the responsible actor, and unauthorized attempts are observable. Events can be retrieved beyond the feed display limit without being overwritten by later state changes.

title: Refresh replay rejection does not revoke the active token family
evidence: security.py:143 stores previous_refresh_token_hash but only queries the current hash when rotating. The isolated probe rejected reuse of the old token while leaving the related session unrevoked. Rotation has no explicit row lock in this code path.
impact: If a refresh credential is stolen and rotated by an attacker, later replay by the legitimate holder does not invalidate the attacker-held successor. Existing expiry, session checks and password fingerprint checks provide useful protections but do not resolve this case.
remediation: Detect replay of prior tokens and revoke the relevant family with an auditable event. Handle concurrent legitimate refresh calls deliberately; test atomic rotation on MySQL. Retain only bounded hashed history.
acceptance: A reused token is rejected and invalidates its family according to the documented policy. Concurrent refresh tests do not leave multiple valid successors or produce uncontrolled 500 responses.

title: Runtime database account has schema-changing privileges
evidence: runtime-privileges.json shows the app identity has CREATE, DROP, ALTER, EVENT, TRIGGER and routine/view privileges on its database, in addition to data access. Global privileges showed USAGE. No database alteration was performed by the audit.
impact: Compromise of the runtime app can have a larger destructive impact than ordinary data reads/writes. Deployment migrations need broader privileges, but every API and worker process does not need to retain those powers.
remediation: Use separate runtime and migration database identities. Reduce runtime grants to demonstrated application requirements, and keep elevated deployment credentials outside ordinary app containers.
acceptance: The app passes its integration suite with reduced grants. Runtime DROP/ALTER/GRANT attempts fail in staging while an authorized migration job can upgrade and validate the schema.

title: Queue durability and long-running worker isolation need validation
confidence: Confirmed configuration; failure behavior not exercised
evidence: Redis reports AOF disabled and successful RDB snapshotting. Celery tasks share the default queue; the worker has concurrency 2. Screenplay calls allow a 900-second timeout with retries. No explicit task time limits or task routing were found in celery_app.py.
impact: A crash can lose work since the last Redis snapshot, and slow AI jobs can delay file scans or notifications. At-least-once redelivery and long tasks require idempotency and timeout alignment. Queue length was zero at the sampled instant; no backlog outage is claimed.
remediation: Define acceptable broker data loss, durable task reconciliation, separate latency-sensitive queues and bounded task execution. Add queue-age alerts and retry/dead-letter handling. Validate Redis visibility timeouts against the longest job. See reference R3.
acceptance: Staging worker/broker restarts preserve or reconcile every accepted job. Duplicate execution does not duplicate business effects. Upload scans and push remain within their service targets while AI workers are busy.

title: Deployed Python packages have outstanding advisory matches
evidence: pip-audit checked 87 third-party installed distributions from an 88-package inventory. It returned 14 records representing 7 distinct IDs in cryptography 49.0.0 and pip 25.0.1. cryptography is constrained below 50 in pyproject.toml, excluding the reported fix.
impact: A vulnerable version match needs reachability triage. The cryptography issue concerns PKCS#7 decryption; app private fields use Fernet and no pkcs7_decrypt call was found. pip issues concern package installation, not an exposed app route. No successful exploitation was demonstrated.
remediation: Review and update to compatible fixed versions, including changing the cryptography upper bound after regression testing. Update the build toolchain and generate a pinned inventory. Record justified non-reachability decisions and scan the rebuilt image.
acceptance: Rebuilt Python inventory has no unresolved actionable advisories. Version exceptions have owners and expiry dates. The full backend suite, encryption round trips and push signing pass with the chosen versions. See references R4-R6.

title: Release reproducibility and supply-chain checks are incomplete
evidence: Dockerfile uses python:3.12-slim without a digest and installs range-constrained dependencies from pyproject.toml. No production Python lock/hash file is used by that build. CI runs tests and coverage, but the inspected workflows do not run dependency/container advisory scans.
impact: Rebuilding the same Git commit can resolve a different runtime. Current deployed image identity is recorded, which helps rollback, but future reproducibility and base-image advisory coverage remain incomplete. The host OS/container OS were not fully vulnerability-scanned in this audit.
remediation: Pin reviewed dependencies and base image digests, retain an SBOM and build provenance, and gate on actionable package/base-image findings. Review action pinning and release approval ownership. Keep the existing 85% combined coverage gate.
acceptance: A clean build is traceable to source and dependency hashes. CI publishes an SBOM, advisory results, tests and immutable image digest. Promotion and rollback use reviewed artifacts, not an uncontrolled rebuild.

title: Privacy, consent and retention procedures lack release evidence
evidence: Registration displays agreement text without a linked policy in the inspected checkbox; auth_controller.dart submits a fixed 2026-07 terms version and backend requires only a nonempty version. Account deletion creates a support request. Retention is described in docs, but no retention task appears in Celery scheduling; 37 expired incomplete uploads remain.
impact: A user request is recorded, but completion, exceptions and deletion across storage/backups are not demonstrated. The report evaluates implementation and operational readiness, not legal compliance or the legal validity of contracts.
remediation: Publish approved, versioned policies and link them at consent points. Validate accepted versions server-side. Implement a staffed deletion/export process and retention jobs with legal-hold exceptions, evidence and service deadlines.
acceptance: Users can read the exact terms they accept. A test deletion/export case completes across relevant stores with a documented retained-data exception list. Retention jobs are monitored and cannot remove held records.

title: Real-browser and device release acceptance remains incomplete
evidence: The fresh CUA inventory returned no browsers/apps and a native pipe startup error. No live UI walkthrough, browser push display, camera/file picker, accessibility or physical-device check was possible. Recent 920 Flutter tests and a web build passed but do not establish these outcomes.
impact: The deployed experience may still have browser-specific navigation, storage, download, permission or accessibility failures. This is a missing sign-off, not a claim that each listed flow is broken.
remediation: Run a recorded browser/physical-device acceptance matrix with ordinary and staff roles after security fixes. Include refresh/logout, mobile widths, keyboard/screen reader, uploads/downloads, notifications, QR links, contracts and interrupted-network recovery.
acceptance: Supported browsers and devices pass the matrix with screenshots/results and no severe defects. A real browser push is displayed and its acknowledgement recorded. Accessibility blockers and permission-denial paths have owners and resolution evidence.

title: Pagination is inconsistent and hides older admin records
evidence: admin_control.py:319 returns the latest 200 users with no cursor/page metadata; production has 240 accounts. Search can find selected older records, but browsing cannot enumerate all users. Safety-check/incident and several specialist lists have no explicit result bound.
impact: Administrators can miss records outside a fixed result cap, while unbounded lists become slow as data grows. Per-user serialization also executes multiple related-count queries. Existing small datasets and passing tests do not prove acceptable production scale.
remediation: Add consistent bounded cursor pagination, totals where useful and matching UI navigation. Batch related counts and define indexes/query budgets. Keep filters and access scopes intact.
acceptance: A dataset larger than each page limit can be fully enumerated without omissions/duplicates. Query counts and response sizes stay bounded and older users/records are reachable in the UI.

title: Uploads lack account storage budgets and type-content validation
confidence: Confirmed source review; abuse load not executed
evidence: verification.py:391 accepts caller-declared allowed MIME values and files up to 250 MiB (25 MiB for KYC). The binary handler enforces byte limits; file_processing verifies checksum and antivirus. No account-wide storage quota or content-signature validation was found in these paths.
impact: Clean but wrongly typed files can enter workflows, and repeated valid uploads can consume the remaining disk. Antivirus is important but does not establish that bytes match an image/PDF label. No malicious or bulk file was uploaded to production.
remediation: Validate file signatures/decoding for each supported purpose, add per-account/project storage budgets and bounded orphan cleanup, and monitor disk reservation. Keep quarantine and ownership gates. Reject unsupported or oversized content before expensive processing.
acceptance: MIME-spoofed files fail safely; valid supported formats still work. Account quotas cannot be bypassed with repeated sessions. Abandoned files expire under retention rules and scanning failures remain private.

title: OpenAPI omits 119 implemented API operations
evidence: openapi-drift.json compares live Flask routes to docs/openapi.yaml after removing /api/v1 and normalizing variable names. There are 390 implemented operations and 271 documented operations; 119 implemented operations are missing and no documented operation is unmatched.
impact: Client developers and security reviewers lack a complete interface contract. This is documentation drift, not evidence that the connected Flutter client fails on those endpoints.
remediation: Update request/response/auth/error schemas for the missing operations and generate a CI route-contract comparison. Document manual payment, notification delivery and visibility semantics explicitly.
acceptance: The normalized operation diff is empty and schema tests cover authentication, error envelopes, pagination and key domain state transitions.

title: Android release configuration still uses debug signing
evidence: android/app/build.gradle.kts:24 and 37 uses applicationId com.example.cineconnect and signingConfigs.getByName("debug") for release. Native store artifacts/signing, iOS release provisioning and store acceptance were not verified in this audit.
impact: The repository is not ready for a production Android store release using this configuration. This finding is conditional on native distribution and does not by itself prevent a secured web-only launch.
remediation: Assign the final package/bundle identity, configure protected release signing and build versioning, and complete platform entitlements, privacy metadata and store/device testing. Keep signing secrets out of Git and general build logs.
acceptance: A signed release AAB/IPA uses the approved identity and certificate/provisioning, installs on supported devices and passes store validation. Recovery and access controls for signing material are documented.

title: Provider-dependent and unsupported features need explicit launch scope
confidence: Confirmed capability state; device delivery unverified
evidence: Live bootstrap: browser push=true with VAPID configured; email=false, SMS OTP=false, liveness=manual_review and social_metrics=self_reported. No native push provider exists. Earlier remediation deliberately disabled unsupported 2FA, biometrics, Urdu, WhatsApp and watermark controls.
impact: Truthful disabled states are an improvement, but these features cannot be advertised as operational. Browser provider acceptance is not proof of visible delivery. Manual KYC and payment verification require staff capacity and defined escalation.
remediation: Approve the supported launch feature list and publish matching UI/help text. Test real browser delivery; configure native/SMS providers only when required by the chosen release. Establish staff workflows for manual services and privileged-account protection.
acceptance: Product claims match tested capabilities. Optional unsupported services are visibly unavailable; required services have real delivery evidence and alerting. Privileged access has an approved MFA or compensating control plan.

title: Capacity, concurrency and end-to-end regression evidence is insufficient
evidence: Fresh HTTP checks were small read-only samples, mostly about 0.38-0.98 seconds from this workstation. No sustained load, soak, failover or payment concurrency test ran. Recent combined coverage is 85.75%, with 90.08% statements but 68.90% branches. New targeted probes exposed eight policy failures despite a green suite.
impact: Passing unit/integration tests does not establish throughput, p95 latency or correct conflict handling under concurrent writes. Test coverage percentages must not be interpreted as a readiness score. AI provider latency and real bank reconciliation were not exercised.
remediation: Add adversarial authorization tests from this report, concurrent payment/refresh/upload cases against MySQL, and a realistic staging load/soak plan. Define user volume, latency, queue age and error-budget targets before selecting capacity.
acceptance: A representative dataset and agreed load meet the documented SLOs without lost/duplicate business effects. All reproduced failures become passing regressions, and failure-recovery tests validate bounded behavior.
